prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (call sign Juniper), primary EMS dispatch: intake, triage, ambulance dispatch, shared incident/unit/access picture; maintains regional coverage picture from unit locations, crew reports, readiness. Zones have primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center; readiness gaps escalated and reassessed after incidents/route changes. Intake creates incident record; caller report preserved. Juniper produces Unit Staging Change Card; records authorization time and unit-selection reason. Actors: Call Taker Mara (Larkspur): location first, repeat-back; produces Caller Location Correction Slip. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield): sets/records priority; escalates to Regional Medical Director (clinical guidance only, no dispatch authority); sends Pediatric Acuity Note. Dispatcher: recommends unit per regional approval rules; states gate/approach constraints and uncertainty; corrects discrepancies by fresh transmission. Shift Commander (Sundial): operational authority, surge, repositioning; reviews coverage picture before approving staging move; must not override clinical policy/crew judgment. Radio Coordinator (Mistral): selects/confirms talkgroup, transmits incident ID, location, priority, assignment, hazards over Regional Radio Network; retries and alerts dispatch supervisor if no acknowledgment; confirms route changes before diversion; sends Coverage Gap Bulletin when coverage below regional threshold. Paramedic Crew: acknowledges with repeat of location/priority; reports route conflicts and status (available, responding, on scene, transporting, unavailable) promptly; stays at staging point until reassigned. Hospital Liaison Desk (Kestrel): destination capabilities, coordinates with Emergency Department; produces Bedside Arrival Receipt. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay): reports vehicle restrictions; verifies maintenance clearance before availability; produces Battery Swap Voucher. Data Quality Officer (Pebble): flags gaps; sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo; no priority changes. Systems: Computer Aided Dispatch Console (details, travel times, staging options); Ambulance Coordination Platform (consolidates unit position/status, matching units); Ambulance Unit 417 (reports position/status entering/leaving staging); Regional Radio Network (instructions, acknowledgments); North Gate Status Board (North Approach Queue Snapshot) and South Gate Status Board (southern access conditions) support routing. Process: triage, resource selection, controlled handoff after crew acknowledgment and confirmed details.

New part:
S137: Shift Commander sends the Mutual Aid Release Form when a neighboring service is released from regional coverage.
S138: Regional Dispatch Center uses the swap voucher to confirm that a unit's battery readiness is current before it is placed in service.
S139: Regional Dispatch Center uses the queue snapshot to account for congestion approaching the northern entry before assigning a route.
S140: North Gate Status Board displays the latest queue condition and access restriction for units approaching the northern entry.
S141: Triage Supervisor advises dispatch when changes in clinical demand may require repositioning available units.
S142: Regional Medical Director establishes clinical priorities that dispatch applies when assigning units during elevated demand.
S143: Hospital Liaison Desk provides receiving-facility capacity information for consideration during transport planning.
S144: Dispatchers compare projected response times with remaining coverage before moving a unit away from its current area.
S145: Data Quality Officer reviews inconsistent location or status reports and routes corrections through the established operational process.
S146: Ambulance Coordination Platform retains time-stamped status changes so supervisors can review the sequence of unit movement.
S147: A crew advises dispatch when a road closure, unsafe condition, or unexpected delay makes the assigned route unsuitable.
S148: Regional Dispatch Center records the approved alternative route and checks that the change does not leave a critical area without reasonable coverage.
S149: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination consultation when a patient’s condition or the operating status of a facility may affect the assignment.
S150: The consultation uses the patient’s reported condition, transport estimate, and current facility acceptance information available to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S151: The Regional Medical Director provides clinical guidance when destination selection involves a specialized capability or a regional care protocol.
S152: The Hospital Liaison Desk contacts the Emergency Department to confirm whether the proposed destination can receive the patient.
S153: The Regional Dispatch Center uses the correction slip to reconcile a reported destination change with the active incident record.
S154: Larkspur confirms the incident identifier and intended receiving facility before the destination request is transmitted.
S155: The Emergency Department advises the Hospital Liaison Desk of relevant capacity limits, access constraints, or changes to its receiving status.
S156: The Hospital Liaison Desk records the consultation outcome and communicates any destination restriction to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S157: The Regional Dispatch Center evaluates the consultation outcome against patient acuity, transport time, and available ambulance coverage.
S158: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents the approved destination and any associated operational instructions to dispatch staff.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
